title: #104 P: PR review, merge, and verified 2.6.0-preview.N publication for Sharedale #162
description:
Objective: land LayeredCraft/cdk-constructs#104 on main through the established review process and make it available
to sharedale/sharedale#162 as a verified, published `2.6.0-preview.N` NuGet package. Each step needs maintainer
authorization (commit/push/PR/merge are not implied by earlier beads).

Steps:
1. PR from a feature branch (conventional title, e.g. `feat(web-function): manage .local companion log group`;
   pr-title-check.yaml). Body: summary, closes #104, design revision 5 link, golden diff summary, sandbox evidence
   (cdkc-18e.18.4), the binary-compat note (D2), and the Sharedale #162 handoff.
2. CI green on the final head (pr-build.yaml: build + tests net8.0-net11.0 + 80% coverage).
3. Codex PR review, then targeted follow-up reviews after each fix round, until no actionable findings remain (same
   process as #103). Record each round and disposition in notes. Re-run CI after fixes.
4. Merge to main (maintainer). Merge includes src/ changes, so Publish Preview triggers (publish-preview.yaml:
   push to main, paths-ignore docs/**, README.md, ROADMAP.md, mkdocs.yml, requirements.txt; reusable
   LayeredCraft/devops-templates publish-preview.yml@v10.8 + nuget-push). Use workflow_dispatch only if the push run
   did not trigger.
5. Verify the actual published version from the run (gh run view <id> --log | grep version / nuget push output). Do
   NOT assume `.28`: the suffix comes from the automation and any other main push (e.g. Dependabot) also publishes.
6. Verify on nuget.org: https://api.nuget.org/v3-flatcontainer/layeredcraft.cdk.constructs/index.json lists the
   version; download the .nupkg and confirm the new API is present (e.g. inspect the assembly/XML doc for the
   companion-retention parameter on WebFunctionLogs.Create and the new assertions), and the nuspec still requires
   Amazon.CDK.Lib >= 2.274.0.
7. Confirm availability from the feed Sharedale consumes (nuget.org; `dotnet package search
   LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs --prerelease --exact-match` or a scratch restore outside both repos).
8. Record the exact version in this bead, cdkc-18e.18, and cdkc-18e.17 notes. Comment on LayeredCraft#104 with the
   version if the maintainer approves (do NOT edit Sharedale issues; the Sharedale maintainer picks it up in #162).

Handoff: sharedale/sharedale#162 cannot begin its construct migration until step 7 passes. Stable 2.6.0 is NOT
published here; it stays gated by cdkc-18e.17 (Sharedale Milestone 12 validation + explicit maintainer approval).

title: #104 S: AWS sandbox validation of companion log-group retention (requires maintainer authorization)
description:
Objective: deployed validation of LayeredCraft/cdk-constructs#104 in the existing Web Functions sandbox
(samples/web-functions/sandbox; design §19.1 style). REQUIRES explicit maintainer authorization and maintainer-provided
NON-PRODUCTION credentials. Do not start without both. Reuse the existing deploy.sh/smoke.sh/destroy.sh flow; do not
build a new sandbox framework.

Preparation (no deploy): add a small log-group check to the sandbox scripts (e.g. smoke.sh/destroy.sh or a helper in
common.sh) using `aws logs describe-log-groups --log-group-name-prefix /aws/lambda/web/` that prints name,
retentionInDays, and storedBytes for each sandbox function. Configure at least one function with non-default
retention for both groups. Pre-check that no `{name}` / `{name}.local` groups exist from earlier runs.

Verify and record (date, Region, CDK/CLI version, library commit, function names, revision IDs, command output):
1. Immediately after deploy and BEFORE traffic: both groups exist, created by CloudFormation, with configured retention.
2. After real requests: both groups still have the configured retention (companion NOT unlimited); events reach the
   centralized group; `.local` holds the same events.
3. No other `.local` group appears for the sandbox functions (e.g. none without retention, none under another name).
4. Use-mode path if the sandbox exercises it (otherwise record "not verified").
5. Teardown: destroy.sh removes both groups (DESTROY); confirm Lambda does not recreate `.local` after stack deletion
   (re-check after a few minutes); record any leftover and clean it by exact name.
Record results in notes and in the implementation PR description (#104 acceptance criterion).
If any check fails: record it, file a bug bead linked to cdkc-18e.18.2, leave this bead open.
Exclusions: production accounts, Sharedale resources, publishing, multi-Region deployment.
acceptance_criteria:
- Checks 1-3 and 5 PASS on live AWS with evidence in notes; check 4 PASS or explicitly "not verified".
- Sandbox fully torn down and verified (no stacks, buckets, roles, distributions, log groups left).
- Results summary pasted into the #104 implementation PR description.

Existing requirements unchanged.

Required: before traffic both groups exist with configured retention; after traffic retention unchanged (companion not unlimited) and events in centralized group; no other .local group; a supplied-role Use(custom) function WITHOUT companion delivers logs (exercises G1 + documented-format G2 CreateLogGroup ARN; else record 'not verified' = G2 ARN form unverified); teardown removes managed groups, no recreation, service-created groups from the Use scenario deleted by exact name. All earlier requirements preserved.

Functions nextjs/aspnetcore/blazor/uselogs/usecompanion Active; revisions rev-ejzpw/rev-gy57c/rev-j19du (smoke) and manual traffic to uselogs/usecompanion 2x HTTP 200 each.

VALIDATION MATRIX (A-G):
A Managed groups/retention PASS: 10/10 groups present pre- and post-traffic with configured retentions 14/3, 14/3, 30/1, 7/none, 14/3; CFN-owned groups match app stack; managed companions created by CFN and present in DependsOn of each revision. Pre-traffic verify exit 0 (phase pre-traffic).

Live ./verify-log-groups.sh --expect-delivery => PASS=31 FAIL=0 SKIP=0 BLOCKED=0. Note: storedBytes reported 0 for all groups despite events; storedBytes is NOT a valid delivery signal (harness bug fixed).
C Use-mode G1/G2 PASS: UseLogs runs with caller-supplied role UseLogsRoleD18EB0C3-uQdw2Y8zm5IN; inline policy statements confirmed in real IAM: logs:CreateLogStream/PutLogEvents on arn:aws:logs:us-east-1:403542860824:log-group:/lccdk-wf-sandbox/wft7d-uselogs:* ; same actions on arn:aws:logs:us-east-1:403542860824:log-group:/lccdk-wf-sandbox/wft7d-uselogs.local:log-stream:* ; logs:CreateLogGroup on arn:aws:logs:us-east-1:403542860824:log-group:/lccdk-wf-sandbox/wft7d-uselogs.local (G2 ARN form CONFIRMED, no :* suffix). AWS accepted the narrowly scoped CreateLogGroup during actual Lambda creation; the group is NOT in the app stack's 9 AWS::Logs::LogGroup resources. G1 delivery confirmed by events in both groups.
D Supplied companion PASS: UseCompanion supplies both groups; role UseCompanionRole462AA494-vlHdMSBgaCuT with G1-only statements (no CreateLogGroup); no duplicate group; supplied retentions preserved; delivery confirmed. Imported/supplied resources correctly not asserted CFN-owned.
E Warnings PASS/SKIP: W1 @layeredcraft/cdk-constructs:webFunctionUnmanagedCompanionLogGroup emitted for UseLogs and captured from cdk.out metadata (build/synth-warnings-wft7d.json). W2 remote-Region warning SKIPPED: no PerRegion/MultiRegion endpoint deployed; extra regions intentionally not deployed per authorization.
F AlreadyExists collision OPTIONAL/SKIP: not run; scope not expanded.
G Teardown PASS: SANDBOX_CONFIRM_DESTROY=wft7d ./destroy.sh --yes => exit 0; app/external/artifacts stacks destroyed and confirmed absent; buckets emptied and deleted; service-created /lccdk-wf-sandbox/wft7d-uselogs.local removed by exact name and confirmed gone. Independent post-destroy verification (build/post-destroy-verification.json): all 3 stacks absent, both buckets 404, zero wft7d Lambda functions/web functions, zero wft7d IAM roles/policies, no CloudFront distribution/OAC references, all 10 log groups absent, prefix scan empty. Delayed recheck after 180s (build/post-destroy-recheck.json): no wft7d log groups/.local groups/layers recreated.

IAM/CFN EVIDENCE: G2 identity statement exactly as documented; UseLogs revision depends only on central group; managed revisions depend on both groups. W1 warning ack ID captured. Evidence paths: build/log-delivery-evidence.json, build/verify-delivery-events-fix.log, build/log-group-summary.json, build/synth-warnings-wft7d.json, build/destroy-wft7d.log, build/post-destroy-verification.json, build/post-destroy-recheck.json; offline suites build/run-scenarios-events-fix.log (110 pass) and build/run-smoke-events-fix.log (44 pass).

ACCEPTANCE: checks 1-3 and 5 PASS with live evidence; check 4 (Use-mode path) PASS; sandbox fully torn down and independently verified. The "results summary in #104 implementation PR description" bullet is deferred to cdkc-18e.18.5 because this authorization forbids creating/pushing a PR; the summary above is ready to paste there. No production-code defect found; the only defect was the sandbox verification script's storedBytes delivery check, now fixed and revalidated offline + live.
Harness state-isolation follow-up (offline suites; no production-construct code touched).

ROOT CAUSE: both offline suites shared sandbox state with the real deployment under samples/web-functions/sandbox/build/ — artifacts.json (manifest), smoke-summary.json, revision-state.json, .smoke/, .verify-log-groups/, log-group-summary.json. The smoke suite's fresh_state deletes the shared manifest/summary, so running the suites concurrently (or after a torn-down deployment whose manifest was removed) corrupted each other's prerequisites and produced non-deterministic failures (post-teardown: run-scenarios 106/110, smoke 42/44; parallel: 108/110, 41/44). No production-construct defect.

CORRECTION: added an overridable SANDBOX_STATE_DIR to common.sh (default ${SANDBOX_DIR}/build, so real-deployment behavior is unchanged) and routed all sandbox-local state through it: MANIFEST_FILE (common.sh), SMOKE_TMP + smoke-summary.json (smoke.sh), VG_TMP + log-group-summary.json (verify-log-groups.sh), revision-state.json + smoke-summary.json (run-workflow.sh). Both offline suites now allocate a private mktemp -d state dir and remove it on exit, isolating fixtures from deployment state and from each other.

VERIFICATION (offline, stubbed aws/cdk; no AWS credentials or mutations): run-scenarios.sh = 110 passed/0 failed and run-smoke-scenarios.sh = 44 passed/0 failed in EVERY configuration tested — concurrent, scenarios-then-smoke, smoke-then-scenarios, and with build/artifacts.json removed beforehand. Real build/ state is untouched after runs (manifest stayed absent, proving isolation). Guarded teardown unchanged (destroy.sh not modified).
close_reason: Live AWS validation in authorized sandbox wft7d passed all mandatory checks (A-E, G) with real AWS evidence; sandbox fully torn down and independently verified absent including the service-created .local group. title: #104 I: Implement companion log group, dependencies, IAM, warnings, assertions, tests and goldens
description:
Objective: implement design revision 5 (spec: docs/designs/lambda-web-functions-integration.md rev 5, §8.3 #revision-5-companion-local-log-groups-104; summary in cdkc-18e.18.1 DESIGN) for
LayeredCraft/cdk-constructs#104, test-first (RED -> GREEN), including XML docs, public Testing assertions, and golden
templates. Do not start until revision 5 is written and approved (cdkc-18e.18.1 notes).

Scope (file : change):
- Models/WebFunctionLogs.cs : Create(retention, removalPolicy, companionRetention = null -> THREE_DAYS);
  Use(logGroup, companion = null) with literal-name validation (ArgumentException "companion"); internal
  CompanionRetention / Companion; XML docs for all three factories (two groups, duplication, short companion retention,
  ServiceDefault = both service-created, unlimited retention, outlive the stack).
- WebFunctionConstruct.cs ResolveLogs (~L211) / ctor (~L55-97):
  * Create: child "LocalLogGroup" named $"{group.LogGroupName}.local", companionRetention, same RemovalPolicy.
  * Public ILogGroup? LocalLogGroup.
  * Ordering: revision Node.AddDependency on both managed groups; in Use mode on each supplied group only when owned
    (Node.DefaultChild is CfnResource) and in the same Stack. No cross-stack/imported dependencies.
  * IAM (design rev 5 §8.3 'Execution-role permissions'): trigger unchanged (ShouldGrantWrite). Keep
    logGroup.GrantWrite(Role). Add via Grant.AddToPrincipal: G1 CreateLogStream+PutLogEvents on
    arn:{p}:logs:{R}:{acct}:log-group:{name}.local:log-stream:*; G2 CreateLogGroup on
    arn:{p}:logs:{R}:{acct}:log-group:{name}.local only when no companion is supplied or any PerRegion/MultiRegion
    endpoint exists (G2 added at most once, guarded by a private flag: in the ctor, or by CreateEndpoint the first
    time a PerRegion/MultiRegion endpoint is created). R = one Lazy.String with a private DeputyBase-derived
    IStableStringProducer reading a private "has non-home endpoint" flag: '*' or Stack.Of(this).Region. Resolved
    at synthesis, so AddEndpoint after construction widens the already-added G1; never mutate a rendered policy or
    an added PolicyStatement (design rev 5 §8.3 'Mechanism'). Stack.FormatArn(COLON_RESOURCE_NAME). Never CreateLogGroup on the centralized
    group, logs:*, or log-group:*. Created-role managed policy unchanged; immutable roles not mutated; GrantInvoke
    classification untouched.
  * W1 AddWarningV2("@layeredcraft/cdk-constructs:webFunctionUnmanagedCompanionLogGroup", ...) for Use w/o companion.
- WebFunctionEndpointConstruct.cs (~L31) + WebFunctionConstruct.CreateEndpoint (~L156): W2
  AddWarningV2("@layeredcraft/cdk-constructs:webFunctionRemoteCompanionLogGroups", ...) on PerRegion/MultiRegion
  endpoints (default + AddEndpoint) with the mode-specific suffix; logging mode passed internally. No diagnostics framework.
- Models/WebFunctionValidation.cs (~L50): reserve "LocalLogGroup".
- Testing/WebFunctionConstructAssertions.cs: ShouldHaveLogGroup(name, retentionDays),
  ShouldHaveCompanionLogGroup(centralizedName, retentionDays), ShouldHaveRevisionDependingOnLogGroups(functionName,
  params logGroupNames); match by name; XML docs; existing assertion signatures unchanged.
- Tests: exactly design rev 5 §15 (T1–T11, P1–P15, Wa–Wg; P11–P15 are the configuration-order regression tests: HomeRegion default + later AddEndpoint(PerRegion) and AddEndpoint(MultiRegion) -> Region '*', exactly one G1 and one G2; several non-home endpoints -> no duplicates; AddEndpoint(HomeRegion) keeps stack Region; env-agnostic -> Ref AWS::Region/AccountId; imported immutable role + non-home AddEndpoint -> no IAM policy, no exception), plus positive/negative tests for each new
  assertion. Place in WebFunctionConstructTests / WebFunctionSecurityTests (permissions) / new tests as fits.
- Goldens: regenerate with UPDATE_GOLDEN_TEMPLATES=1 and review every diff: Create goldens gain only the .local group
  + DependsOn; web-function-use-log-group gains revision DependsOn on its same-stack group + the companion statement
  in the supplied role's policy. Existing-construct goldens: zero diff (no regeneration).

Risk to verify, not assume: G2 uses the documented log-group ARN format (no ':*'); sandbox check 3.9
(cdkc-18e.18.4) confirms. If revision-5 review changes this, follow the doc.

Exclusions: user docs/CHANGELOG (cdkc-18e.18.3); sandbox (cdkc-18e.18.4); no cross-Region resources, custom
resources, adoption/import of existing groups, new NuGet deps, reflection; centralized default name/retention unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:

- Use contract: optional companion, name validation, W1 when absent, same-stack-only dependencies (T6–T9).
- ServiceDefault unchanged in template; XML docs updated (T10).
- IAM: P1–P15 pass, including the explicit configuration-order regressions P11–P15 (HomeRegion default then
  AddEndpoint(PerRegion|MultiRegion) yields Region '*' G1 and G2 in the final template, no duplicates; immutable

  Lambda may create it), Region = stack Region or '*' with PerRegion/MultiRegion; CdkUpgradeGuard_* unchanged and passing.

title: #104: Manage Web Function .local companion log group with finite retention
description:
LayeredCraft/cdk-constructs#104: manage the Lambda Web Function `.local` companion log group with finite retention, so no
library consumer is left with an unowned, never-expiring log group. Must ship in a `2.6.0-preview.N` package before stable
2.6.0 (gate cdkc-18e.17). Downstream consumer: sharedale/sharedale#162 (Milestone 12) cannot start its construct migration
until a preview containing this work is published and verified.

Verified AWS behavior (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/web-functions-logging.html, -permissions.html):
- Companion name = centralized name + ".local", for default (/aws/lambda/web/{fn}) AND custom groups.
- `.local` is written in every Region where requests run, including the home Region; centralized group is home Region only.
- Lambda creates either missing group on first use with default settings (never expire). It never removes events from
  `.local` after centralization; retention is per group. Docs: "create the log group and its `.local` companion yourself
  before you route traffic to the revision." No documented way to disable the companion.
- Execution role needs logs:CreateLogStream/PutLogEvents on BOTH `arn:aws:logs:{home}:{acct}:log-group:{name}:*` and
  `arn:aws:logs:*:{acct}:log-group:{name}.local:*` (Region wildcard). "If the role cannot write to the `.local` log group in
  a Region, Lambda does not deliver logs from that Region."
- Live Tail with least delay runs on `.local` in the serving Region; centralization typically within minutes.

Current library (src/LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs/WebFunctionConstruct.cs ResolveLogs ~L211, Models/WebFunctionLogs.cs):
- Create(retention=TWO_WEEKS, removal=DESTROY) creates only `/aws/lambda/web/{FunctionName}` (child id `LogGroup`);
  revision DependsOn it. No companion.
- Use(ILogGroup) passes the name; ShouldGrantWrite grants write on the centralized group only when name is outside
  /aws/lambda/* (GAP: no `.local` grant -> with a supplied mutable role and a custom group, logs are not delivered at all).
  No revision dependency on a same-stack supplied group with a literal name.
- ServiceDefault(): nothing created; XML/docs mention only the default group.
- No non-HomeRegion logging annotation; no log-group assertions in Testing/.

Children: design addendum -> implementation (+tests/goldens/helpers) and docs -> AWS sandbox validation -> PR/review/
merge/preview publication. Stable release is NOT part of this feature (stays in cdkc-18e.17).

Out of scope (issue #104): non-home-Region log-group creation, changing centralized default name/retention, log-level/
metric/subscription helpers, adoption/import machinery for existing service-created groups, Sharedale changes.

title: T3c: Correct IAM grant, resource-policy, and endpoint-import review findings
description:
Purpose: correct the confirmed findings of the independent T1–T3b implementation review before T4 builds on them. Design: docs/designs/lambda-web-functions-integration.md REVISION 4. Authoritative sections: §8 (namespace note), §8.3 (reserved child IDs, read-only Endpoints, execution-role ordering), §8.4 (AddToResourcePolicy restrictions, imported-endpoint validation and account rule), §10.2 (updated table + "Revision 4 corrections" items 1–6), §10.3 (statement integrity), §12.1, §14 (revision-4 rows), §15 (revision-4 additions), §21 revision 4.

Implement revision 4 exactly. If any rule cannot be implemented as written (for example a CDK public API behaves differently from what the design states), STOP and record a blocker with bd update <id> --append-notes. Do not change the design yourself.

Deliverables (files: WebFunctionGrants.cs, WebFunctionEndpointConstruct.cs, WebFunctionImportedEndpoint.cs, WebFunctionConstruct.cs, Models/WebFunctionEndpoint.cs → move, tests):

1. F1 Service principals (§10.2 rev-4 item 1). GrantInvoke throws InvalidOperationException for any principal whose PolicyFragment.PrincipalJson is a "Service" principal (bare ServicePrincipal or PrincipalWithConditions wrapping one), under BOTH CallerPolicy values. The service name is a token in CDK 2.274, so resolve it (Stack.Of(endpoint).Resolve) to detect cloudfront.amazonaws.com. Remedy text: CloudFront → "use GrantCloudFrontInvoke(distributionArn)"; other services → "add an explicit, condition-scoped statement with endpoint.AddToResourcePolicy(...)". Do NOT add aws:SourceAccount automatically. Do NOT add a new public API for scoped service grants (deferred).
2. Wildcards (§10.2 rev-4 item 2; §8.4).
   - GrantInvoke throws InvalidOperationException for EVERY wildcard principal (PrincipalJson AWS="*" or LiteralString="*"; AnyPrincipal, StarPrincipal, OrganizationPrincipal, conditioned or not) under both CallerPolicy values. Remedy text: use an explicit, conditioned AddToResourcePolicy statement.
   - AddToResourcePolicy rejects (ArgumentException) Allow statements that have no conditions and name a wildcard or service principal, and Allow statements using NotPrincipal.
   - Deny statements are unrestricted.
   - An explicit Allow with a wildcard AND conditions is accepted. Check only that conditions are present; do NOT build any IAM-condition analyzer. XML docs state the consumer is responsible for the conditions meaningfully restricting access.
   - GrantCloudFrontInvoke (conditioned) keeps working.
3. F3 Account principals (§10.2 rev-4 item 3). AccountPrincipal and AccountRootPrincipal (by .NET type), and any principal whose LITERAL AWS principal is an account root ARN, are never established. Automatic throws, even for the same account. ExternallyManaged behavior unchanged.
4. P1 Verified identity writes (§10.2 rev-4 item 4) for owned AND imported principals. The identity side counts as written only when (a) the grant principal is a concrete owned mutable CDK identity (.NET Amazon.CDK.AWS.IAM.Role, User, Group, or LazyRole with Resource.IsOwnedResource == true), or (b) AddToPrincipalPolicy returned StatementAdded == true with PolicyDependable is Amazon.CDK.AWS.IAM.Policy (replacing the current "is IConstruct" check). Everything else is not written: fallback to the resource statement on an owned endpoint, throw on an imported endpoint. Never infer a write from Grant.PrincipalStatements. Verified facts on 2.274.0: an owned Role returns an EMPTY DependencyGroup (so signal (b) alone would break owned roles); ImmutableRole returns an empty DependencyGroup; imported mutable role/user/group return Policy; a classic Function's role, LazyRole, and User surface as concrete .NET types; owned.WithoutPolicyUpdates() surfaces as an IPrincipal proxy (not Role).
5. F2 Role dependency (§8.3 notes, §12.1). Replace _revision.Node.AddDependency(Role) with a dependency on the role's CfnRole only (Role.Node.DefaultChild when it is a CfnResource; nothing extra for imported roles; ExecutionRoleArn already references the role). Never depend on the DefaultPolicy subtree. Keep every other DependsOn edge (Function, created LogGroup, bucket PolicyDependable).
6. F5 Imported endpoints (§8.4; public API addition approved by the maintainer).
   - Add `public string? Account { get; init; }` to WebFunctionEndpointAttributes, with XML docs.
   - Validation:
     - a literal EndpointArn must match arn:{p}:lambda:{r}:{12 digits}:web-function/{fn}/endpoint/{ep} (ArgumentException);
     - a literal DomainName must be non-empty (null → ArgumentNullException, empty → ArgumentException);
     - a literal Account must be 12 digits;
     - when Account and the ARN are both literal, they must be equal (ArgumentException);
     - tokens are not validated.
   - Environment: Env.Account = the literal ARN account, else Account; Env.Region from the ARN. Use ResourceProps.EnvironmentFromArn, or explicit Account/Region if CDK does not allow combining them. Assert the result in tests either way.
   - Endpoint account = the literal ARN account, else a literal Account; anything else is NOT established.
   - If the endpoint account is not established, GrantInvoke throws for EVERY grantee, owned included (this replaces the revision-3 owned-only rule and its annotation). The message names both remedies (supply a literal Account; configure caller access outside this app) and notes that the endpoint remains usable as a CloudFront origin with ExternallyManaged origin permissions.
   - If the endpoint account is established, a grantee is established only when its account is literally SAME (owned → its stack account; imported → PrincipalAccount). ONE_UNRESOLVED and BOTH_UNRESOLVED are not established.
   - Constructing an imported endpoint with a token ARN and no Account must succeed; it must not throw at FromEndpointAttributes.
7. P6 Statement integrity (§10.3). AddToResourcePolicy validates, then stores statement.Copy() with Freeze() applied. WebFunctionConstruct registers a node validation that returns PolicyDocument.ValidateForResourcePolicy() errors for the resource policy (when one exists). Keep StatementAdded/PolicyDependable return semantics.
8. P3 Reserved ids (§8.3). AddEndpoint throws ArgumentException for the ids Function, Revision, DefaultEndpoint, ExecutionRole, LogGroup, ResourcePolicy (ordinal).
9. Endpoints read-only. Return a cached ReadOnlyCollection (or equivalent) that cannot be cast back to a mutable List; the public type stays IReadOnlyList<WebFunctionEndpointConstruct>.
10. F4 Diagnostics (§10.2 rev-4 item 6). Errors and annotations identify the grantee by the IGrantable's construct path when it is an IConstruct (jsii IRole proxies are), else the principal's resolved policy-fragment JSON, else the type name. Identify the endpoint by construct path + EndpointName, never by an ARN token. No human-facing text contains "${Token[". The ExternallyManaged annotation describes caller-side identity policies only for IAM identities.
11. Namespace (§8 rev-4 note). Move IWebFunctionEndpoint to namespace LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs, in file IWebFunctionEndpoint.cs at the project root. XML docs state it is not intended for consumer implementation. Also correct the stale WebFunctionConstruct XML summary ("added by later releases").

Regression tests (WebFunctionInvokeGrantTests / WebFunctionResourcePolicyTests / WebFunctionConstructTests; [Collection("CDK Tests")]; assert on templates and messages, not on internals):
- Service principals: cloudfront (message names GrantCloudFrontInvoke), another service, and a conditioned one each throw under Automatic AND ExternallyManaged; no ResourcePolicy synthesized.
- Wildcards:
  - GrantInvoke with AnyPrincipal, StarPrincipal, and a conditioned OrganizationPrincipal throws under BOTH policies; no ResourcePolicy is created.
  - AddToResourcePolicy: an unconditioned "*" Allow throws; Allow+NotPrincipal throws; a Deny with "*" is accepted; an explicit Allow with "*" plus an aws:PrincipalOrgID StringEquals condition writes exactly that statement (condition preserved).
- Same-account AccountPrincipal and AccountRootPrincipal under Automatic throw.
- No-op identity writes (real CDK types, no fakes): Role.FromRoleArn(Mutable=false); Mutable=false + AddGrantsToResources=true; owned.WithoutPolicyUpdates(). Each → resource statement with the role ARN principal, ZERO AWS::IAM::Policy, and returned Grant.PrincipalStatements empty; the same grantees on an imported endpoint throw.
- Real identity policies: owned Role, classic Lambda Function, WebFunctionConstruct, mutable imported role, imported User, imported Group → exactly one AWS::IAM::Policy statement with Action lambda:InvokeWebFunctionEndpoint and Resource = that endpoint's ARN, attached to the right role/user/group; no ResourcePolicy.
- Unresolved imported ARNs: token role ARN (Fn.ImportValue) and a literal role ARN in an env-agnostic stack under Automatic → throw, zero AWS::IAM::Policy.
- Imported endpoints:
  - Throw at FromEndpointAttributes: an invalid literal ARN (a function ARN, a missing endpoint segment); null and empty DomainName; a non-12-digit Account; an Account that differs from a literal ARN's account.
  - A literal ARN with an equal Account is accepted.
  - Env.Account/Env.Region equal the endpoint's (literal ARN; token ARN + literal Account).
  - A literal foreign ARN with an owned caller in an env-agnostic stack throws.
  - A token ARN with no Account: construction succeeds, and GrantInvoke throws for an owned Role AND for an imported mutable role, with ZERO AWS::IAM::Policy.
  - A token ARN with a literal Account equal to the caller stack's account and an owned caller writes the identity policy.
  - A token ARN with a literal Account different from the caller's account throws.
  - An immutable same-account role on an imported endpoint throws.
- CDK upgrade guard: group the real-CDK principal-behavior tests (no-op writes, real identity policies, service/wildcard/account classification) in a clearly named class or trait (e.g. CdkPrincipalBehaviorRegressionTests). description:
Purpose: CloudFront origin factory with OAC and automatic, same-stack permission granting. Design §5.4, §8.5, §9.4, §9.7, §11.1 (AUTHORITATIVE steps), §11.2 (spike results), §12.3, §14, §15 (CloudFront/OAC).

Deliverables (src/LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs/WebFunctionOrigin.cs + internal origin class):
- public static class WebFunctionOrigin:
  * WithOriginAccessControl(IWebFunctionEndpoint, WebFunctionOriginWithOacProps? = null): throws immediately for ApplicationManaged endpoints.
  * WithoutOriginAccessControl(IWebFunctionEndpoint, WebFunctionOriginProps? = null): throws for IamAuth endpoints; returns an HTTPS HttpOrigin.
- internal sealed class WebFunctionOacOrigin : DeputyBase, IOrigin (jsii interface implemented from .NET; proven by spike) whose Bind(scope, options):
  1. Signing: HomeRegion/PerRegion → Signing.SIGV4_ALWAYS_AMZ_AUTH; MultiRegion → new Signing(SigningProtocol.SIGV4A, SigningBehavior.ALWAYS_AMZ_AUTH).
  2. OAC: use supplied IOriginAccessControl unchanged (not inspected), else create one L2 FunctionUrlOriginAccessControl with child id "WebFunctionOac" in the bind scope. No CfnOriginAccessControl.
  3. Permissions Automatic: imported endpoint → throw; Stack.Of(scope) != Stack.Of(endpoint) → throw with the same-stack/dependency-cycle message and ExternallyManaged remedy;
     else endpoint.GrantCloudFrontInvoke(Stack.Of(scope).FormatArn({Service="cloudfront", Region="", Resource="distribution", ResourceName=options.DistributionId})).

- GrantInvoke algorithm (§10.2): throw for ApplicationManaged; identity side ONLY when the account is established:
  E1 = grant principal is an owned construct (Resource.IsOwnedResource) whose stack account is not literally different from the endpoint stack's;
  E2 = imported principal with literal PrincipalAccount equal (TokenComparison.SAME) to the literal endpoint stack account.
  Resource side when: identity side not written for an established same-account immutable role; service principal; or CallerPolicy = ExternallyManaged.
  Under Automatic, fail with InvalidOperationException (grantee, endpoint, reason, two remedies) for: imported principals with any unresolved account (ONE_ or BOTH_UNRESOLVED),
  different literal account, AccountPrincipal/ArnPrincipal. ExternallyManaged never writes identity policy and adds an Annotations info naming the required caller-side identity policy.
- WebFunctionEndpointConstruct.FromEndpointAttributes(scope, id, WebFunctionEndpointAttributes) → IWebFunctionEndpoint that owns nothing: identity grants for established (E1/E2) grantees only;
  any grant requiring the resource policy, ExternallyManaged grants, and GrantCloudFrontInvoke throw ("resource policy of an imported endpoint is externally owned").
  Parse endpoint name/account/region from a literal ARN; token ARN ⇒ unresolved account (only E1 grantees can be granted).

same under ExternallyManaged → resource statement + annotation; different literal account Automatic throws / ExternallyManaged resource-only with no principal statements in returned Grant;

title: AWS Lambda Web Functions support — LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs
description:
Implement AWS Lambda Web Functions support in LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs per the APPROVED design (revision 3):
docs/designs/lambda-web-functions-integration.md (authoritative; GitHub issue #98).

Scope: new additive constructs WebFunctionConstruct, WebFunctionEndpointConstruct/IWebFunctionEndpoint, WebFunctionOrigin,
WebFunctionCode.FromBucket, WebFunctionLogs, supporting models, Testing helpers, docs, and a mandatory AWS sandbox release gate.

Non-negotiable constraints (design §2, §6, §8, §10.2, §12.4):
- Hybrid composition; L3 over CDK L1 (CfnWebFunction/Revision/Endpoint, CfnResourcePolicy); no upstream alpha/L2 dependency;
  upstream L2 types never appear in the public API.
- Existing constructs (LambdaFunctionConstruct, StaticSiteConstruct, DynamoDbTableConstruct, CognitoUserPoolConstruct) are
  NOT modified; their synthesized templates must not change (golden templates from cdkc T0).
- Explicit AuthType on every endpoint (no default). Single-owner resource policy per function. Same-stack automatic OAC
  permissions only. Limited endpoint imports (no whole-function import). Existing S3 artifacts only (no FromAsset).
  Default log retention TWO_WEEKS. No customer-managed revision KMS key. Workload-neutral (Next.js, ASP.NET Core shim,
  Blazor Static SSR) with no workload-specific constructs.
- GrantInvoke follows the revision-3 algorithm in §10.2 (account establishment E1/E2, Automatic vs ExternallyManaged).
  Never use Grant.AddToPrincipalOrResource or trust Grant.Success/AssertSuccess.
- Amazon.CDK.Lib floor 2.274.0.

Rules for every implementation agent:
- Implement only the claimed bead's scope. If the design is ambiguous or seems wrong, stop and record a blocker note on
  the bead (bd update <id> --append-notes ...) instead of changing the design.
- Do not commit, push, open PRs, publish NuGet packages, or close GitHub issue #98 unless separately authorized by the maintainer.

title: T2 follow-up: Harden owned code-bucket inspection (tokens, unrecognized values, DSSE classification)
description:
Purpose: align WebFunctionCodeFromBucket.ValidateOwnedBucketConfiguration (src/LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs/Models/WebFunctionCode.cs) with design §14 and the revision-4 clarification under the §14 table. Source: independent review findings P4 and DSSE.

Defects:
(1) Tokens are rejected instead of skipped: a VersioningConfiguration.Status token resolves to {Ref:...}, its ToString() is compared to 'Enabled', and the bucket is rejected.
(2) A Stack.Resolve result whose structure is not recognized should be treated as unknown and skipped, not rejected.
(3) UsesAwsManagedKey rejects every aws:kms:dsse bucket, including DSSE with a customer-managed key. Per §8.7/§14, reject only DSSE_MANAGED (no key) and KMS_MANAGED/aws/s3, and make each message name the actual problem.
(4) Versioning enabled only through an escape-hatch property override is a documented limitation, not a fix target. T6a documents the workaround (Bucket.FromBucketName + ExternallyManaged).

Keep the current rule that owned buckets are inspected even under ExternallyManaged; the design does not change that.

Tests: token Status skipped; DSSE with a customer key accepted; DSSE_MANAGED rejected with an accurate message; KMS_MANAGED still rejected; customer-key SSE-KMS accepted; unversioned still rejected.

Exclusions: IAM/grant code (T3c), docs (T6a). No golden changes expected; verify. No commits or pushes unless authorized.
acceptance_criteria:
• Unresolved bucket configuration values are handled conservatively: a token or unrecognized versioning Status, encryption algorithm, encryption structure, or KMS key id is SKIPPED and never rejected (each case has a test). Unresolved values are never treated as proof of a violation.
• Literal violations are still rejected: unversioned, KMS_MANAGED/aws/s3, DSSE_MANAGED (no key).
• DSSE with a customer-managed key is accepted. Messages name the actual problem.
• Escape-hatch-only versioning remains a documented limitation (T6a); it is not handled in code.
• New tests pass; all goldens unchanged.
• Release build has 0 warnings and the full suite passes on net8.0–net11.0; evidence is recorded in notes.
notes:
Maintainer decision (2026-10-23): keep escape-hatch S3 versioning as a documented limitation. Handle unresolved values conservatively: never reject tokenized values.
IMPLEMENTATION (2026-10-23): Rewrote WebFunctionCodeFromBucket.ValidateOwnedBucketConfiguration in src/LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs/Models/WebFunctionCode.cs into ValidateVersioning + ValidateEncryption + ValidateKmsKey, classifying every value as literal-valid, literal-invalid, or unresolved/unrecognized.

Storage/versioning/encryption handling:
- Versioning: missing VersioningConfiguration or literal Status "Suspended" -> reject (VersioningMessage). Literal Status "Enabled" -> accept. A token Status, a missing status key, a non-dictionary resolved structure, or any other literal status -> skipped (never rejected).
- Encryption: missing BucketEncryption -> no violation. Unrecognized structure (not a map, no rules, no ServerSideEncryptionByDefault) -> skipped. Algorithm literal "aws:kms": key literal aws/s3 or empty/absent -> reject (KmsManagedMessage names aws/s3); literal customer key -> accept; token/absent-as-token key -> skipped (never treated as AWS-managed). Algorithm literal "aws:kms:dsse": no key / aws/s3 -> reject (DsseManagedMessage names customer-managed key); literal customer key -> accept; token key -> skipped. AES256 and any other literal algorithm -> accepted.
- LiteralString helper returns null for a non-string value or a string containing `${Token[`, so resolved tokens are never misread as literals.

Security-policy behavior: ExternallyManaged still inspects owned buckets (versioning/encryption) exactly as before - design §14 row unchanged. The Automatic-only cross-stack account/Region guard and AddToResourcePolicy remain bypassed under ExternallyManaged (no bucket-policy statement is generated). No other semantics changed.

Regression tests added to test/LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs.Tests/WebFunctionConstructTests.cs (13 new): enabled+S3-managed accepted (asserts synthesized S3::BucketPolicy); disabled (Versioned=false) rejected with versioning message; suspended rejected; tokenized versioning Status skipped (asserts synthesized policy); unrecognized literal versioning Status skipped; AWS-managed KMS (aws/s3) rejected naming aws/s3; customer-managed KMS accepted; tokenized KMS key skipped; DSSE with customer-managed key accepted; DSSE_MANAGED rejected naming customer-managed; DSSE + aws/s3 rejected; unrecognized encryption structure skipped; ExternallyManaged cross-stack owned bucket with unresolved function env does not throw (Automatic-only guard not applied). Existing fixtures retained (owned-bucket policy statements + revision DependsOn on bucket policy, imported-bucket Automatic error, ExternallyManaged no-policy, unversioned, KMS_MANAGED, cross-stack Automatic error). These exercise the real L1 property structs (CfnBucket.VersioningConfigurationProperty / BucketEncryptionProperty) so validation runs against synthesized configuration.

Evidence: dotnet build -c Release -> Build succeeded, 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s). Full suite per TFM (dotnet run --project test/LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs.Tests/ -c Release --no-build): net8.0/net9.0/net10.0/net11.0 each Total 450, Errors 0, Failed 0, Skipped 0 (was 437 before; +13). All 24 golden templates byte-identical (git reports no GoldenTemplates changes); no golden updates required. dotnet format --verify-no-changes reports no issues in the two changed files. Only two files modified. No commit or push performed (per task restrictions).

Unresolved behavior (documented, not code): versioning enabled solely via an escape-hatch property override is not detected (limitation, T6a workaround); imported buckets remain uninspected.

- Workload recipes (same page or docs/examples/web-functions.md): Next.js standalone; ASP.NET Core via Node.js execve shim (self-contained linux-arm64 apphost "server", index.js
  `process.execve("/var/task/server", ["/var/task/server"], process.env);`, Kestrel on http://$AWS_LAMBDA_HTTP_ENDPOINT, readiness POST to
  http://$AWS_LAMBDA_RUNTIME_API/2025-09-01/ready after start, app-local ICU or invariant globalization, no HTTPS redirection/HSTS); Blazor Static SSR (same shim; untrimmed server;
  ContentRootPath = AppContext.BaseDirectory when AWS_LAMBDA_HTTP_ENDPOINT is set; wwwroot/_framework shipped; cache fingerprinted assets; Interactive Server/Auto/legacy Blazor Server

Also document (derived from design §8.2 + §12.1, found during planning): with WebFunctionCodeBucketPolicy.Automatic the code object must exist before the revision is created, so in practice the owned bucket must live in a separately deployed stack (deploy bucket stack -> upload artifact -> deploy function stack). A bucket created in the same stack as the function cannot be pre-populated.
REVIEW ROUTING (2026-10-23, design revision 4). Add to docs/constructs/web-function.md:
(1) Log-group switching: moving an EXISTING function from WebFunctionLogs.ServiceDefault() to Create(), or redeploying after stack deletion while /aws/lambda/web/{name} still exists, fails with AlreadyExists because Lambda auto-creates the group. Document the remedies: Use(LogGroup.FromLogGroupName(...)), or delete/import the group.
(2) CDK 2.274 emits F3006 'Unknown resource type AWS::Lambda::WebFunction*' validation warnings, which become synthesis ERRORS when @aws-cdk/core:validateAgainstDefaultRules is enabled. Document the acknowledgement IDs (CloudFormation-Validate::F3006) and the consequence.
(3) GrantInvoke rejects service principals (CloudFront → GrantCloudFrontInvoke; other services → explicit condition-scoped AddToResourcePolicy) and unconditioned wildcards; same-account AccountPrincipal is not 'complete'.
(4) The revision no longer waits for execution-role DefaultPolicy statements; a brief IAM-propagation window can occur on first deploy.
(5) Owned-bucket limitation: versioning enabled only by an escape-hatch override is not detected; workaround Bucket.FromBucketName + ExternallyManaged.
(6) IWebFunctionEndpoint is not intended for consumer implementation.
Maintainer clarification (2026-10-23):
(7) Conditioned wildcard resource-policy statements are supported only through explicit AddToResourcePolicy. The consumer is responsible for ensuring the conditions meaningfully restrict access; the library checks only that conditions are present.
(8) Imported endpoints: document the optional Account attribute. GrantInvoke needs an established endpoint account (literal ARN or literal Account); a token-ARN endpoint is still usable as an ExternallyManaged OAC origin.
From T4 independent review (F1): document the IOrigin.Bind exception behavior. Exceptions thrown inside IOrigin.Bind (and inside CDK's HttpOrigin constructor) cross the jsii boundary and surface to .NET callers as System.Exception carrying the original message (e.g. "connectionAttempts: Must be an int between 1 and 3 (inclusive); received 5."), whereas WebFunctionOrigin factory-time validation (auth mismatch, nulls) throws InvalidOperationException directly.
